ov: A large, mostly nocturnal forest antelope of sub-Saharan Africa with a chestnut coat, 10–15 thin white stripes and heavy spiral horns on both sexes. The lowland bongo lives in the forests of West and Central Africa; the rare mountain bongo survives only in central Kenya.

why.et: Hunted for its hide, horns and meat, and a common local source of bushmeat.
why.ac: A large, mostly nocturnal forest antelope.

rg: Forests of West and Central Africa, from Sierra Leone and Guinea to the Congo basin and South Sudan, plus a few mountains in central Kenya.
df: Leaves, bushes, vines, bark, roots, cereals and fruit; it visits salt licks and even eats burnt wood for minerals.
fx: The third-largest antelope in the world.
There may be as few as 140 mountain bongos left in the wild, fewer than in zoos.
